local.prompt: Create one wide 16:9 scientific observer illustration for Fidelity: hypothetical local surface view on Titan, Saturn's moon. Independently invent a low flat pebble-strewn plain with softly rounded centimetre-scale-looking stones and a few shallow drainage-like depressions; this is NOT the Huygens landing site or any observed terrain. Do not copy or recolour Moon, Mars, Pluto, any planet map or any existing photograph. Low viewpoint over subdued ochre-brown material under deep amber diffuse daylight in thick nitrogen/methane aerosol haze. Soft shallow shadows and rapidly lost contrast toward a hazy level horizon; no blue sky, no stars, no visible Sun disk, no visible Saturn or rings. No liquid puddles, active rain, plants, life, plume, ocean, spacecraft, astronaut or survivable-landing implication. Stone chemistry, material proportions, morphology, lighting, colour, exposure and haze appearance are all invented illustrative assumptions; do not suggest measured local fractions or calibrated colour. Water ice identity at the Huygens landing site is inconclusive in DISR spectra, so do not label stones as proven water ice. No photoreal satellite/global-map insets. Elegant educational composition with usable central scene. At upper-left put exact clearly readable small but legible text 'IMAGINED · TITAN LOCAL VIEW'. At lower-left put exact text 'Invented terrain · haze and colour uncalibrated'. These are the only words. Preserve ample image area, naturalistic cinematic texture but restrained light; no oversharpening or dramatic mountains.
local.inspection: Inspected independent ochre pebble plain, invented shallow depressions and amber haze. Clear IMAGINED TITAN LOCAL VIEW and invented-terrain/uncalibrated-haze-colour text. No Saturn, rings, stars, Sun disk, spacecraft, organism or surface liquid. Rocks and shadow/exposure remain invented; texture is not a measured site or Huygens reconstruction.

paper.title: The reflectance spectrum of Titan’s surface at the Huygens landing site determined by the Descent Imager/Spectral Radiometer
paper.datesLimit: PDF footer separately says ©2017 and preprint submitted November7,2018; retain these inconsistent document dates, not a new observation or corrected journal date.

terms.scope: Linked arXiv record grants distribution only; not blanket CC BY.

assessment.finding: Reconstruction uses measured calibration-lamp flux and finds higher reflectance than earlier flux-ratio methods. Authors interpret the change as an opposition effect; calibration, geometry and surface heterogeneity alternatives remain discussed.

Visible red slope and near-IR blue slope are spectral results; the1500nm feature has competing tholin/water-ice interpretations. DISR evidence for water ice is explicitly inconclusive, not a local measured material fraction.

Atmospheric methane4.5±0.5% inferred by absorption-band modelling, sensitive to coefficient choices; not a universal Titan terrain/material abundance. Surface liquid methane layer unsupported in these spectra; shallow wet soil is not excluded.
Diffuse illumination and phase sensitivity prevent treating a publisher landing JPEG as an independently calibrated visible-colour global map. No new sky/raster size computation performed.
